title: Distinguish a real residual intervention from terminal phase subtraction
statement: For the specified finite g,lambda,gamma,gamma_up>0 model, every fixed nonzero residual loses logical off-diagonal coherence, whereas delta=0 protects it exactly and delta=O(1/T) retains a signed readout. Terminal phase subtraction does not reproduce that evolution. For the separate perfect-clock terminal-quadrature family with logical dephasing gamma_L>0, conditional KL<=Delta² total_time/(4gamma_L) yields the stated inverse-square precision lower bound only for 0<alpha<1/2. The noiseless two-point lower bound separately needs W>=4epsilon and matches the precision exponent, not the confidence logarithm.

requires: For fixed-residual decay: the stated finite auxiliary model with all positive listed rates
For the lower bound: fresh logical inputs, terminal binary quadrature, perfect clock, common initialization and no free informative old calibration
Causal references/durations/phases, deterministic total interrogation budget and 0<alpha<1/2

This is not arbitrary-material metrology, a full-record/channel equivalence or superiority over an equally supplied ordinary controller.
